propositions: A drainer process dying between O_EXCL lock creation and release leaves a 0-byte file permanently, causing all subsequent drain attempts to fail with FileExistsError and skip enrichment silently at INFO level without any error signal.

The drain lock has no owner stamp, no pid liveness check, and no age-based reclaim mechanism, unlike the store's mkdir write lock which has all three, allowing dead-holder locks to wedge enrichment indefinitely.

When a stale drain lock is detected (via extracted _stamp_is_stale core with unrecognised_via_ceiling=True), it must be reclaimed with exactly one bounded retry and logged at WARNING with holder name and age to make the wedge visible.
An unstamped 0-byte orphan lock older than the CEIL must be reclaimable, while locks created within the window must be respected to avoid breaking concurrent create-and-stamp sequences.
The drain lock must be stamped with v2 owner format (host=/ns=/pid=/start=) on acquisition and the stamp must remain byte-identical when a live holder is refused during reclaim collision.

rebar doctor's drain-leg lock report must decode the v2 stamp and report a real staleness verdict (stale-lock/not-stale) instead of not-assessable, with dead-holder locks surfacing as findings at exit 1.
